formality: Formal, professional register. Prefer impersonal/infinitive phrasing for UI chrome (buttons, labels, status text) over direct address. Where direct address to the user is unavoidable (account/session messages, confirmations), use formal 'Pan/Pani' conjugation, not the informal 'ty' — this is professional pentest/security tooling used across teams and client engagements, not a consumer app.
styleNotes: Keep hashcat/security jargon that has no natural Polish equivalent in English (per doNotTranslate and the keepEnglish-flagged terms below) rather than coining awkward neologisms — this matches how Polish security professionals actually talk. Button and action labels use the imperative verb form ('Zastosuj', 'Archiwizuj', 'Zamontuj'), never a bare noun or infinitive. Translated nouns keep correct Polish gender/number agreement on any adjective built from them — 'hasz' is masculine ('złamany hasz', plural 'złamane hasze'), 'reguła'/'maska' are feminine. 'job' (zadanie) and 'task' (podzadanie) must stay visibly different strings in the UI even though both derive from the same root — they are different levels of the scheduling model and collapsing them to one word creates ambiguity.

hash.note: Singular noun; Polish security professionals often use 'hasz' or keep 'hash' depending on context. Use 'hasz' in UI.

hashlist.note: Feminine noun; refers to the uploaded password hash collection

hash type.note: Refers to the hashcat mode designation (e.g., NTLM, SHA256)

cracked.note: Adjective, cited in masculine singular (dictionary form); agrees with the noun in gender/number: 'złamany hasz', 'złamana reguła', plural 'złamane hasze'.

cracked hashes.note: Plural of 'hasz' (masculine-inanimate plural takes '-e': 'hasze', not 'hashe'); refers to recovered hash:plaintext pairs.

potfile.note: hashcat-specific filename; industry standard kept as English

wordlist.note: Dictionary file of candidate passwords. 'Wordlista' is the Polonized borrowing Polish pentesters actually use ('wordlista do ataku słownikowego'), parallel to 'hasz'/'maska'; literal 'lista słów' is an understandable but less idiomatic alternate.

rule.note: Feminine noun; hashcat password mangling rule; 'reguły' plural

mask.note: Feminine noun; hashcat mask pattern like ?u?l?l?d; Polish security pros use 'maska'

charset.note: Custom character set for masks; Polish: 'zestaw znaków' or 'charset' kept in some contexts

attack mode.note: Masculine noun; refers to straight, combination, brute-force, or hybrid modes

brute force.note: 'Brute force' is kept as the compound technical term (same treatment as 'potfile'/'webhook') rather than forced into an awkward literal 'atak siłowy'; only 'atak' is translated.

keyspace.note: Total candidate count for an attack; 'przestrzeń kluczy' or sometimes kept as 'keyspace'

chunk.note: Feminine noun; a slice of job keyspace assigned to one agent; 'porcja' or 'porcja zadania'

task.note: Deliberately NOT 'zadanie' (that's 'job') — this is the chunk-level assignment running on one agent. Keeping it as 'podzadanie' (sub-task) avoids the UI showing the identical word for two different levels of the scheduling model. 'jedno podzadanie na agencie'.

job.note: Neuter noun; a cracking job against a hashlist. Kept distinct from 'task'→'podzadanie' so the two scheduling levels don't collide on the same Polish word.

workflow.note: Ordered sequence of preset jobs; 'przepływ pracy' or 'workflow' in technical context

loopback.note: Re-run attack with newly cracked passwords until dry; 'pętla zwrotna' (feedback loop) captures the iterative re-run. Avoid 'logowanie zwrotne' — that reads as 'reverse login' and has nothing to do with this feature.

max agents.note: Maximum agents a job may use; shortened: 'maks. agentów'

overflow.note: Extra agents beyond the limit; masculine noun; 'nadmiar agentów'

benchmark.note: hashcat speed test for a hash type on an agent

hash rate.note: Throughput metric (hashes computed per second, hashcat's H/s figure) — independent of whether anything is actually cracked, so avoid 'szybkość łamania' ('cracking speed'), which wrongly implies a success rate. 'Hashrate' is the term Polish GPU/cracking communities actually use, kept English like 'potfile'.

progress.note: Masculine noun; how much of the keyspace is completed; 'postęp zadania'

agent.note: Machine running KrakenHashes agent and hashcat; English term standard in Polish security tech

device.note: Neuter noun; a GPU/CPU on an agent; feminine in some contexts: 'karta graficzna'

claim code.note: One-time or reusable code to register an agent

voucher.note: Same product concept as 'claim code' per the source glossary — use the identical Polish term so the UI doesn't look like it has two different registration mechanisms. Do not translate this separately as 'kod dostępu'.

heartbeat.note: Periodic agent check-in. Polish networking/ops usage keeps 'heartbeat' in English (same treatment as 'ping', 'keep-alive') rather than the unnatural literal 'sygnał życia'.

offline buffer.note: Grace period before an agent is marked offline; 'bufor offline' mirrors the English term order and reads naturally as a settings label (e.g. 'Bufor offline (s)'). Longer paraphrase 'okres przed oznaczeniem offline' is fine in help text.

auto-update.note: Feminine noun; automatic agent binary update; can abbreviate to 'auto-aktualizacja'

binary.note: hashcat binary version managed by server; neuter noun; informal: 'binarka'

client.note: Masculine noun; customer/engagement the hashlists belong to

team.note: Masculine noun; group of users sharing clients, hashlists and agents

member.note: Masculine noun; user in a team; feminine form 'członkini' if applicable

owner.note: Masculine noun; user an agent or resource belongs to; feminine: 'właścicielka'

retention.note: Matches the standard Polish RODO/GDPR phrase 'okres przechowywania danych' for a data-retention period. Bare 'przechowywanie' reads as 'storage', not specifically the retention-period setting.

archive.note: This is a UI action (hide from default lists without deleting), so the glossary form is the imperative button verb, consistent with 'apply'→'zastosuj'. Noun form: 'archiwum'; infinitive: 'archiwizować'.

analytics report.note: Adjective form is the natural Polish compound for this kind of report (cf. 'raport analityczny' in Polish BI tools); genitive 'raport analizy' reads as a literal, less idiomatic translation.

password reuse.note: Same password used by several accounts; neuter noun 'użycie'

hash reuse.note: Same hash appearing for several accounts; neuter noun 'użycie'

complexity.note: Feminine noun; password character-class complexity; 'złożoność hasła'

entropy.note: Feminine noun; password entropy in bits; technical term kept similar to English

domain.note: Feminine noun; Windows/AD domain of an account; 'domena AD'

username.note: Feminine noun; account name; also 'login' in Polish

audit log.note: Masculine noun; security event log; 'log audytu' also used

dashboard.note: Home overview page; masculine noun; established Polish software term (e.g. Power BI); 'panel' or 'dashboard' sometimes kept

settings.note: Neuter plural noun; configuration pages; 'preferencje' when referring to user preferences

autosave.note: Saved automatically when leaving a field; neuter noun; 'auto-zapis' (shorter form)

certificate.note: Masculine noun; server TLS certificate; 'certyfikat serwera'

SAN.note: Subject Alternative Name on certificate; technical acronym kept as English

network share.note: Masculine noun; SMB/NFS share for wordlist storage. This is the established term from Polish Windows localization; 'zasób sieciowy' also acceptable

mount.note: This is a UI action (attach a network share to a path), so the glossary form is the imperative button verb, consistent with 'apply'→'zastosuj' and 'archive'→'archiwizuj'. Infinitive 'montować' / perfective 'zamontować'; status once attached: 'zamontowany'.

cloud fleet.note: Rented cloud GPU instances; the prepositional 'w chmurze' reads more naturally than the genitive chain 'instancji chmury'. Shorter adjective form 'flota chmurowa' works where space is tight.

provisioning.note: Starting cloud instances automatically; neuter noun 'inicjowanie'; 'aprowizacja' (alternate seen in some translated cloud docs)

budget.note: Masculine noun; monthly cloud spending limit; 'budżet miesięczny'

threshold.note: Masculine noun; percentage of budget triggering action; 'próg budżetu'

drain.note: Admin-initiated graceful state: stop assigning new work to an agent, let its running tasks finish. 'Opróżnianie' (draining, process noun) fits a status badge ('Opróżnianie…'); action-button imperative is 'Opróżnij'. Avoid 'wyczerpanie' ('exhaustion/depletion') — it reads as a passive negative state, not a deliberate admin action.

teardown.note: Destroying a cloud instance; 'likwidacja' is the term actually used in Polish cloud/infra operations ('likwidacja zasobów'). 'Rozebranie' is literal 'disassembly' and reads oddly applied to a software instance. Verb: 'likwidować'.

webhook.note: HTTP callback for notifications; technical term kept as English in Polish security industry

two-factor authentication.note: MFA; neuter noun; also 'uwierzytelnianie dwuczynnikowe'. In practice Polish UIs most often just keep the acronym '2FA' untranslated rather than using a Polish abbreviation — don't invent one (there is no established Polish abbreviation like 'UDF').

backup codes.note: Masculine plural noun; one-time MFA recovery codes; also 'kody odzyskiwania'

authenticator app.note: TOTP app; feminine noun; also 'aplikacja TOTP'

session.note: Feminine noun; logged-in browser session; 'sesja logowania'

API key.note: Masculine noun; personal key for HTTP API; 'klucz dostępu API'

branding.note: Custom app name, colours and logo. 'Branding' is a fully assimilated loanword in Polish business/marketing usage, and matches KrakenHashes's own 'Branding' settings tab. Literal 'znakowanie' means physical marking/labelling and doesn't carry the brand-identity sense.

diagnostics.note: Feminine noun; troubleshooting/debug tools page; 'narzędzia diagnostyki'
